semantic_checks: kernel_neg follows exact linearity of the oriented interval integral, with no regularity or sign premise introduced.

kernel_mono requires t>=0 and continuous F,G; the positive exponential factor preserves pointwise inequality and continuity supplies integrability on the compact interval. It does not assert order under reversed time.
kernel_const gives the exact constant-forcing solution (K/c)*(1-exp(-c*t)) for c!=0, proved via actual zero initial state and scalar ODE derivative, not from a supplied solution equality.
kernel_const_le is valid for c>0,K>=0 even for negative t, because the omitted term (K/c)*exp(-c*t) is nonnegative. Subsequent comparison bounds correctly still require t>=0.
kernel_le_of_le compares to the actual constant-forcing kernel, then bounds by K/c. The bound F<=K is required throughout [0,t], not only at its endpoint.

abs_kernel_le applies the upper comparison to both F and -F, using exact kernel_neg, and obtains the two-sided absolute bound. Continuous F,c>0,K>=0,t>=0 and the interval absolute input bound are all explicit.
